opening.text: A carpenter does not pick up just any tool. He picks the one that fits the job. God did the same when He needed someone to begin the Restoration. He chose a farm boy from New York. Not because Joseph Smith was perfect, but because he was willing.

mainMessage.text: Joseph Smith was a prophet of God. He was chosen, he was tested, and he gave everything to bring the gospel back.

blocks.text: **Chosen long before** A prophet named Joseph, who lived in ancient Egypt, saw this latter-day Joseph. He even knew his father's name.
For Joseph truly testified, saying: A seer shall the Lord my God raise up, who shall be a choice seer unto the fruit of my loins.

And his name shall be called after me; and it shall be after the name of his father. And he shall be like unto me; for the thing, which the Lord shall bring forth by his hand, by the power of the Lord shall bring my people unto salvation.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
Jesus Christ chose a holy man, a righteous man, to lead the Restoration of the fulness of His gospel.
God's plans are older than we are.
**An obscure boy** Joseph had little schooling and little money. When he told what he saw, people turned on him.

I soon found, however, that my telling the story had excited a great deal of prejudice against me among professors of religion, and was the cause of great persecution, which continued to increase; and though I was an obscure boy, only between fourteen and fifteen years of age, and my circumstances in life such as to make a boy of no consequence in the world, yet men of high standing would take notice sufficient to excite the public mind against me, and create a bitter persecution; and this was common among all the sects— all united to persecute me.

It caused me serious reflection then, and often has since, how very strange it was that an obscure boy, of a little over fourteen years of age, and one, too, who was doomed to the necessity of obtaining a scanty maintenance by his daily labor, should be thought a character of sufficient importance to attract the attention of the great ones of the most popular sects of the day, and in a manner to create in them a spirit of the most bitter persecution and reviling. But strange or not, so it was, and it was often the cause of great sorrow to myself.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
The good spoken of Joseph Smith came slowly; the evil speaking began immediately.
He was a boy of no importance to the world. God saw it differently.
**He brought forth a book** Joseph received the gold plates and translated them by the gift and power of God.
And after having received the record of the Nephites, yea, even my servant Joseph Smith, Jun., might have power to translate through the mercy of God, by the power of God, the Book of Mormon.

He said there was a book deposited, written upon gold plates, giving an account of the former inhabitants of this continent, and the source from whence they sprang. He also said that the fulness of the everlasting Gospel was contained in it, as delivered by the Savior to the ancient inhabitants;
Elder Lawrence E. Corbridge of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Prophet Joseph Smith” from the April 2014 general conference.
There is no dispute about what Joseph Smith accomplished, only how he did what he did and why.
The book is real. The only question is where it came from.
**A voice for his day** Joseph received revelations. The Lord told the Church to listen to His prophet.

Wherefore, meaning the church, thou shalt give heed unto all his words and commandments which he shall give unto you as he receiveth them, walking in all holiness before me; For his word ye shall receive, as if from mine own mouth, in all patience and faith. For by doing these things the gates of hell shall not prevail against you; yea, and the Lord God will disperse the powers of darkness from before you, and cause the heavens to shake for your good, and his name’s glory.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Presidency of the Seventy said this in his talk “A Choice Seer Will I Raise Up” from the October 2016 general conference.
Because Joseph was a prophet, revelations and prophets are no longer a thing of the past.
Heaven did not go quiet again.
**Tested in the dark** Joseph was jailed in Liberty, Missouri, in the winter. The Lord told him that even this would be for his good.

And if thou shouldst be cast into the pit, or into the hands of murderers, and the sentence of death passed upon thee; if thou be cast into the deep; if the billowing surge conspire against thee; if fierce winds become thine enemy; if the heavens gather blackness, and all the elements combine to hedge up the way; and above all, if the very jaws of hell shall gape open the mouth wide after thee, know thou, my son, that all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
I testify that Joseph Smith was an honest and virtuous man, a disciple of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Hard times did not break his faith.
**He gave his life** Joseph and his brother Hyrum were killed in 1844. Their testimony still stands.

Joseph Smith, the Prophet and Seer of the Lord, has done more, save Jesus only, for the salvation of men in this world, than any other man that ever lived in it. In the short space of twenty years, he has brought forth the Book of Mormon, which he translated by the gift and power of God, and has been the means of publishing it on two continents; has sent the fulness of the everlasting gospel, which it contained, to the four quarters of the earth; has brought forth the revelations and commandments which compose this book of Doctrine and Covenants, and many other wise documents and instructions for the benefit of the children of men; gathered many thousands of the Latter-day Saints, founded a great city, and left a fame and name that cannot be slain. He lived great, and he died great in the eyes of God and his people; and like most of the Lord’s anointed in ancient times, has sealed his mission and his works with his own blood; and so has his brother Hyrum. In life they were not divided, and in death they were not separated!
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Presidency of the Seventy said this in his talk “A Choice Seer Will I Raise Up” from the October 2016 general conference.
Because Joseph was a prophet, we have more than a window into heaven—the very doorway to the eternities is open to us.
What he gave us is still open.

story.title: God looks on the heart

blocks.text: When Samuel looked for the next king, he judged by height and looks. God corrected him.

But the Lord said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
The world looked at a poor farm boy. God looked at his heart. He does the same with us.

blocks.text: **The first witness: an ancient prophet** The first witness is very old. A prophet named Joseph spoke of a latter-day seer in a very specific way.
For Joseph truly testified, saying: A seer shall the Lord my God raise up, who shall be a choice seer unto the fruit of my loins.

Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
Jesus Christ chose a holy man, a righteous man, to lead the Restoration of the fulness of His gospel.
The call came from heaven.
**The second witness: his own words** Joseph wrote plainly about being a boy of no standing. He never pretended to be anything else.

Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.

He told the truth even when it did not flatter him.
**The third witness: the Book of Mormon** The book stands on its own. It teaches of Christ on nearly every page.
And after having received the record of the Nephites, yea, even my servant Joseph Smith, Jun., might have power to translate through the mercy of God, by the power of God, the Book of Mormon.

Elder Lawrence E. Corbridge of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Prophet Joseph Smith” from the April 2014 general conference.

For Joseph truly testified, saying: A seer shall the Lord my God raise up, who shall be a choice seer unto the fruit of my loins.

And his name shall be called after me; and it shall be after the name of his father. And he shall be like unto me; for the thing, which the Lord shall bring forth by his hand, by the power of the Lord shall bring my people unto salvation.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
Jesus Christ chose a holy man, a righteous man, to lead the Restoration of the fulness of His gospel.
The path was God's idea.
**A guide of no standing** Joseph was not a scholar or a leader of men. He was a farm boy.

I soon found, however, that my telling the story had excited a great deal of prejudice against me among professors of religion, and was the cause of great persecution, which continued to increase; and though I was an obscure boy, only between fourteen and fifteen years of age, and my circumstances in life such as to make a boy of no consequence in the world, yet men of high standing would take notice sufficient to excite the public mind against me, and create a bitter persecution; and this was common among all the sects— all united to persecute me.

It caused me serious reflection then, and often has since, how very strange it was that an obscure boy, of a little over fourteen years of age, and one, too, who was doomed to the necessity of obtaining a scanty maintenance by his daily labor, should be thought a character of sufficient importance to attract the attention of the great ones of the most popular sects of the day, and in a manner to create in them a spirit of the most bitter persecution and reviling. But strange or not, so it was, and it was often the cause of great sorrow to myself.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
The good spoken of Joseph Smith came slowly; the evil speaking began immediately.
God does not need the world's approval to choose.
**Marker one: the Book of Mormon** The first great marker is a book that points to Christ.
And after having received the record of the Nephites, yea, even my servant Joseph Smith, Jun., might have power to translate through the mercy of God, by the power of God, the Book of Mormon.

He said there was a book deposited, written upon gold plates, giving an account of the former inhabitants of this continent, and the source from whence they sprang. He also said that the fulness of the everlasting Gospel was contained in it, as delivered by the Savior to the ancient inhabitants;
Elder Lawrence E. Corbridge of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Prophet Joseph Smith” from the April 2014 general conference.
There is no dispute about what Joseph Smith accomplished, only how he did what he did and why.
Follow it and you will find Christ.
**Marker two: living revelation** The Lord told His people to listen to His servant as to Himself.

Wherefore, meaning the church, thou shalt give heed unto all his words and commandments which he shall give unto you as he receiveth them, walking in all holiness before me; For his word ye shall receive, as if from mine own mouth, in all patience and faith. For by doing these things the gates of hell shall not prevail against you; yea, and the Lord God will disperse the powers of darkness from before you, and cause the heavens to shake for your good, and his name’s glory.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Presidency of the Seventy said this in his talk “A Choice Seer Will I Raise Up” from the October 2016 general conference.
Because Joseph was a prophet, revelations and prophets are no longer a thing of the past.
The markers are renewed by each new prophet.
**Marker three: faithfulness** Some markers are made of character. Joseph's faith in the darkest hour is one.

And if thou shouldst be cast into the pit, or into the hands of murderers, and the sentence of death passed upon thee; if thou be cast into the deep; if the billowing surge conspire against thee; if fierce winds become thine enemy; if the heavens gather blackness, and all the elements combine to hedge up the way; and above all, if the very jaws of hell shall gape open the mouth wide after thee, know thou, my son, that all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joseph Smith” from the October 2014 general conference.
I testify that Joseph Smith was an honest and virtuous man, a disciple of the Lord Jesus Christ.
We follow his example when we hold on in hard times.
**Marker four: his testimony** His life ended with his brother Hyrum at his side. His witness remains.

Joseph Smith, the Prophet and Seer of the Lord, has done more, save Jesus only, for the salvation of men in this world, than any other man that ever lived in it. In the short space of twenty years, he has brought forth the Book of Mormon, which he translated by the gift and power of God, and has been the means of publishing it on two continents; has sent the fulness of the everlasting gospel, which it contained, to the four quarters of the earth; has brought forth the revelations and commandments which compose this book of Doctrine and Covenants, and many other wise documents and instructions for the benefit of the children of men; gathered many thousands of the Latter-day Saints, founded a great city, and left a fame and name that cannot be slain. He lived great, and he died great in the eyes of God and his people; and like most of the Lord’s anointed in ancient times, has sealed his mission and his works with his own blood; and so has his brother Hyrum. In life they were not divided, and in death they were not separated!
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Presidency of the Seventy said this in his talk “A Choice Seer Will I Raise Up” from the October 2016 general conference.
Because Joseph was a prophet, we have more than a window into heaven—the very doorway to the eternities is open to us.
The path is open. We only need to walk it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about facing something big with only a small amount of strength. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: David and the name of the Lord

blocks.text: David was a shepherd boy. He faced a giant with no armor.

Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
David did not rely on size or skill. He relied on God. Joseph Smith did the same. We can too.

application.text: First, name one step of faith you need to take. Second, ask Heavenly Father for the strength to take it. Third, take the step this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Joseph Smith was called of God. I know the trail he marked leads to Jesus Christ. I am thankful to walk it. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to name one step of faith you need to take.
I invite you to ask Heavenly Father for the strength to take it.
I invite you to take the step this week.
blessings: You will move forward in faith.
You will follow the pattern of the Prophet.

closingVerse.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
